cap_confirmation: driver level_cap=48; Masquerain 46 (0), Ariados 47 (+1), Lokix 47 (+1), Orbeetle 47 (+1) all equal cap+authored offset-2. PASS.
pass_kind: rerun after +1 on Masquerain and Ariados
party_reuse_justification: Unchanged party from receipt 1; stage-legal for this window and the availability audit in the manifest still holds.

attempts.notes: Shorter than the first run but it cost the player's Mega. Ariados's Rage Powder pulled a Flare Blitz off Masquerain twice while Masquerain banked two Quiver Dances; Metagross was then switched in and killed by Lokix's First Impression plus a +2 Bug Buzz before it could Mega Evolve. Incineroar finished at 18/194.

strategy_checks.check: Ariados Rage Powder redirects for the setup partner
strategy_checks.evidence: Rage Powder on turns 1, 2 and 3. It pulled Incineroar's turn-2 Flare Blitz (which was aimed at a 53 HP Masquerain) onto itself, and did it again on turn 3. This is the authored redirection shell working exactly as written.

strategy_checks.check: Masquerain uses the bought turns to Quiver Dance
strategy_checks.evidence: Quiver Dance selected on turns 1 and 2, resolving on turn 2 to +1 and reaching +1 SpA/SpD/Spe; the boosted Bug Buzz then contributed to killing Metagross on turn 4.
Sticky Web was NEVER chosen - zero occurrences in the run log. Ariados spent all three of its turns on Rage Powder. See the dedicated finding below.

strategy_checks.check: Lokix First Impression / Tinted Lens pressure
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 4 First Impression on the incoming Metagross, turn 5 Sucker Punch; the First Impression was the larger half of the Metagross KO.
Turn 5 Light Screen went up before it was Spored.

sticky_web_finding: Sticky Web was not set at any point. Ariados chose Rage Powder on every turn it had, which was individually correct each time - it was protecting a Masquerain that was mid-setup, and the redirection twice absorbed a Flare Blitz that would have ended the setup. But it means the authored hazard never appears, and with only four opposing Pokemon and a battle that lasts five turns there is realistically never a turn where Sticky Web beats Rage Powder. The move is effectively dead weight on this set as authored. Flagged, not fixed - this pass does not change moves.
ai_observations: Amoonguss being Grass-typed made it immune to both Rage Powder redirection and its own team's powder problems, which is why the player's Sludge Bombs kept reaching Masquerain while Incineroar's Fire attacks were siphoned onto Ariados. The AI's redirection choice was right; it simply could not cover both attackers.
could_this_be_cooler: Sticky Web on Ariados never competes with Rage Powder in a four-Pokemon doubles fight. Replacing it with a second redirection-support tool, or moving the hazard to a member that is not the team's redirector, would make the slot real. Not changed in this pass.
